questions.q:
If for some $x \in R$, the frequency distribution of the marks obtained by $20$ students in a test is:

Marks 2 3 5 7
Frequency distribution \left(x + 1\right)2$ \left(2x - 5\right)$ $x^{2} - 3x$ $x

Then the mean of the marks is :

$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Total students $= 20$

$⇒ {\left(x + 1\right)}^{2} + \left(2x - 5\right) + \left(x^{2} - 3x\right) + x = 20$

$⇒ x^{2} + 2x + 1 + 2x - 5 + x^{2} - 3x + x = 20$

$⇒ 2x^{2} + 2x - 24 = 0 ⇒ x^{2} + x - 12 = 0$

$⇒ x = - 4, 3 \left(∵ x > 0\right)$

$∴ x = 3$

Average $= $\dfrac{{\left(x + 1\right)}^{2} \times 2 + \left(2x - 5\right)3 + 5\left(x^{2} - 3x\right) + 7 \times x}{20}

$= $\dfrac{32 + 3 + 0 + 21}{20} =$2.8$

Hence, required mean is~$2 . 8

$

questions.q: If the mean deviation about median for the number $3, 5, 7, 2k, 12, 16, 21, 24$~arranged in the ascending order, is~$6$ then the median is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Median is the central value (or middle observation) of statistical data if it is arranged in ascending or descending order.

Thus, if there are $n$~observations (variates) ${x}_{1}, {x}_{2}, {x}_{3}, \ldots , {x}_{n}$ arranged in ascending or descending order, then

median~$= \left(\dfrac{n + 1}{2}\right)th$~observation, if~$n$~is odd

and median~$= \dfrac{\dfrac{n}{2}\text{th observation} + \left(\dfrac{n}{2} + 1\right)\text{th observation}}{2}$, if~$n$~is even.

Here we can see there are~even number of terms,

So, median~$= \dfrac{2k + 12}{2} = k + 6$

Mean deviation~$= ∑ \left|{x}_{i} - M\right|n = 6$

$⇒ \dfrac{\left(k + 3\right) + \left(k + 1\right) + \left(k - 1\right) + \left(6 - k\right) + \left(6 - k\right) + \left(10 - k\right) + \left(15 - k\right) + \left(18 - k\right)}{8} = 6$

$⇒ \dfrac{58 - 2k}{8} = 6$

$⇒ k = 5$

So, median~$= \dfrac{2 \times 5 + 12}{2} = 11$

questions.q: The mean and variance of $7$~observations are $8$ and $16$ respetively. If two observations are $6$ and $8,$~then the variance of the remaining $5$ observations is :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let $a, b, c, d, e$ be $5$ unknown observations.

Given that No. of observation,~$n = 7,$~Mean $= 8,$~Variance $= 16$

$∴$ sum of observations $= No . ofobservation \times Mean = 7 \times 8 = 56$

$⇒$ Mean of $5$~remaining observations $= \dfrac{56 - 8 - 6}{5} = \dfrac{42}{5}$

As, we know that,

Variance for~$7$~observations$= \dfrac{Σ{x}_i^{2}}{n} - \left(\overset{¯}{x}\right)2$

$⇒ 16 = \dfrac{Σ{x}_i^{2}}{7} - 64$

$⇒ Σ{x}_i^{2} = 560$

$⇒ a^{2} + b^{2} + c^{2} + d^{2} + e^{2} + 64 + 36 = 560$

$⇒ a^{2} + b^{2} + c^{2} + d^{2} + e^{2} = 460$

Variance of remaining $5$ observations $= \dfrac{Σ{x}_i^{2}}{n} - \left(\overset{¯}{x}\right)2 = \dfrac{460}{5} - \left(\dfrac{42}{5}\right)2 = \dfrac{536}{25}$

questions.q: The mean and the median of the following ten numbers in increasing order $10, 22, 26, 29, 34, x, 42, 67, 70, y$ are $42$ and $35$ respectively, then $\dfrac{y}{x}$& is equal to:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Since, number of observations are even $n = 10$

Hence, the median is~$= \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{n}{2}\right)thterm + \left(\dfrac{n}{2} + 1\right)thterm}{2} = \dfrac{{5}^{th}term + {6}^{th}term}{2}$

Thus, median $= \dfrac{34 + x}{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{34 + x}{2} = 35$

$⇒ x = 36 . . . \left(i\right)$

And, mean$= $\dfrac{sumofterms}{numberofterms}

$⇒ $\dfrac{10 + 22 + 26 + 29 + 34 + x + 42 + 67 + 70 + y}{10} =$42$

$⇒ x + y + 300 = 420$

$⇒ x + y = 120 . . . \left(ii\right)$

Put the value of $x$~from \left(i\right)$~in \left(ii\right),$~to get

$36 + y = 120$

$⇒ y = 84$

$⇒ \dfrac{y}{x} = \dfrac{84}{36} = \dfrac{7}{3} .

$

questions.q: Let $S$~be the set of all values of ${a}_{1}$~for which the mean deviation about the mean of $100$ consecutive positive integers ${a}_{1}, {a}_{2}, {a}_{3}, \ldots . , {a}_{100}$ is $25$ . Then $S$ is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

${a}_{1}$ ~be any natural number~

So,~${a}_{1}, {a}_{1} + 1, {a}_{1} + 2, \ldots . , {a}_{1} + 99$~are values of ${a}_{i}$~or observation.

Now mean of the observation is given by,

$\overset{¯}{x} = \dfrac{{a}_{1} + \left({a}_{1} + 1\right) + \left({a}_{1} + 2\right) + \ldots . + {a}_{1} + 99}{100}$

$⇒ \overset{¯}{x} = \dfrac{100{a}_{1} + ( 1 + 2 + \ldots . . + 99 )}{100}$

$⇒ \overset{¯}{x} = {a}_{1} + \dfrac{99 \times 100}{2 \times 100}$

$⇒ \overset{¯}{x} = {a}_{1} + \dfrac{99}{2}$

Mean deviation about mean$= \dfrac{{∑}_{i = 1}^{100}\left|{x}_{i} - \overset{¯}{x}\right|}{100}$

$= \dfrac{2\left(\dfrac{99}{2} + \dfrac{97}{2} + \dfrac{95}{2} + \ldots . + \dfrac{1}{2}\right)}{100}$

$= \dfrac{1 + 3 + \ldots . + 99}{100}$

$= \dfrac{\dfrac{50}{2} [ 1 + 99 ]}{100}$

$= 25$

So, it is true for every natural no. ' ${a}_{1}$ ' as there is no term of~${a}_{1}$& in mean deviation.

questions.q: The first of the two samples in a group has $100$ items with mean $15$ and standard deviation $3 .$~If the whole group has $250$ items with mean $15 . 6$~and standard deviation $\sqrt{13 . 44},$& then the standard deviation of the second sample is:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We have, number of terms in the first group& ${n}_{1} = 100$~with their mean ${X}_{1} = 15$~and~number of terms in whole group is~${n}_{1} + {n}_{2} = 250$~and their mean~$X = 15 . 6 .$

Variance of first group${V}_{1}\left(x\right) = 9$~and whole group is~$Var \left(x\right) = 13 . 44 .$

Now,~${σ}^{2} = \dfrac{{n}_{1}{σ}_{1}^{2} + {n}_{2}{σ}_{2}^{2}}{{n}_{1} + {n}_{2}} + \dfrac{{n}_{1}{n}_{2}}{\left({n}_{1} + {n}_{2}\right)2}\left(\overset{¯}{x}1 - \overset{¯}{x}2\right)2$

and~${n}_{2} = 150, \overset{¯}{x}2 = 16, {V}_{2} ( x ) = {σ}_{2}$

Therefore,~$13 . 44 = \dfrac{100 \times 9 + 150 \times {σ}_{2}^{2}}{250} + \dfrac{100 \times 150}{\left(250\right)2} \times 1$

$⇒ {σ}_{2}^{2} = 16$

$⇒ {σ}_{2} = 4$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Mean& $\overset{¯}{x} = \dfrac{a + 6 + 8 + 5 + 10}{5} = 6$~(given)~

$⇒ a + b = 7 . . . \left(i\right)$

Variance~$= $\dfrac{∑ {x}_i^{2}}{n} - \left(\overset{¯}{x}\right)$2 = \dfrac{a^{2} + b^{2} + {8}^{2} + {5}^{2} + {10}^{2}}{5} - {6}^{2} =6 . 8$~(given)

$⇒ a^{2} + b^{2} = 25 . . . \left(ii\right)$

on solving equations~ \left(i\right)$~&~ \left(ii\right)$, we get~$a = 3, b = 4$

Now, Mean deviation about Mean~$M = $\dfrac{∑ \left|{x}_{i} - \overset{¯}{x}\right|}{n}

$⇒ $\dfrac{\left|3 - 6\right| + \left|4 - 6\right| + \left|8 - 6\right| + \left|5 - 6\right| + \left|10 - 6\right|}{5}

$⇒ $\dfrac{3 + 2 + 2 + 1 + 4}{5} = \dfrac{12}{5}

$∴ M = $\dfrac{12}{5}$⇒ 25M = 60$.

$

questions.q: Let \(x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_{10}\) be ten observations such that \(\sum_{i=1}^{10}\left($x_i-2\right)=30, \sum_{i=1}^{10}\left($x_i-$\beta\right)^2=98, $\beta\gt$2\), and their variance is \($\frac{4}{5}$\). If \(\mu\) and \($\sigma^2\) are respectively the mean and the variance of \(2\left($x_1-1\right)+4 $\beta$\), \(2\left($x_2-1\right)+4 $\beta, \ldots .,$2\left($x_{10}-1\right)+4 $\beta$\), then \($\frac{\beta \mu}{\sigma^2}$\) is equal to :$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \sum_{l=1}^{10}\left(x_l-2\right)=30 \\
& \sum_{i=1}^{10} x_l=50 \\
& \Rightarrow \text { Mean }=5 \\
& \text { Variance }=\frac{4}{5}=\frac{\sum x_l^2}{10}-(\bar{x})^2 \\
& \frac{4}{5}=\frac{\sum x_l^2}{10}-25 \\
& \Rightarrow \sum x_l^2=258
\end{aligned}$
Now, $\sum_{l=1}^{10}\left(x_l-\beta\right)^2=98\begin{aligned}
& \sum_{l=1}^{10} x_l^2-2 \beta \sum_{l=1}^{10} x_l+10 \beta^2=98 \\
& \Rightarrow 258-2 \beta(50)+10 \beta^2=98 \\
& \Rightarrow 10 \beta^2-100 \beta+160=0 \\
& \Rightarrow \beta^2-10 \beta+16=0 \\
& \Rightarrow \beta=8 \text { as } \beta \gt 2
\end{aligned}$
Now, as per the question
$2\left(x_1-1\right)+4 \beta, 2\left(x_2-1\right)+4 \beta, \ldots 2\left(x_{10}-1\right)+4 \beta$
Can be simplified as
$2 x_1+30,2 x_2+30, \ldots, 2 x_{10}+30\begin{aligned} & \mu=2(5)+30=40 \\ & \sigma^2=2^2\left(\frac{4}{5}\right)=\frac{16}{5} \\ & \frac{\beta \mu}{\sigma^2}=\frac{8 \times 40}{\frac{16}{5}}=100\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The mean of $6$ distinct observations is $6 . 5$~and their variance is $10 . 25 .$ If~$4$ out of $6$ observations are $2, 4, 5$~and $7,$ then the remaining two observations are:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let the other two observations be& $a$~and~$b$, then

$\dfrac{a + b + 2 + 4 + 5 + 7}{6} = 6 . 5$

$⇒ a + b = 21$

$⇒ b = 21 - a$

Then, other two numbers are~$a$~and~ \left(21 - a\right)$

Now, variance is~$10 . 25$, therefore

$10 . 25 = \left(4 + 16 + 25 + 49 + a^{2} + \left(21 - a\right)2\right)6 - \left(6 . 5\right)2$

$⇒ 6\left(10 . 25\right) + 6\left(6 . 5\right)2 = 94 + a^{2} + \left(21 - a\right)2$

$⇒ a^{2} + \left(21 - a\right)2 = 221$

$∴ a = 10$~and \left(21 - a\right) = 21 - 10 = 11$

So, remaining two observations are $10, 11.

$

If mean $= \dfrac{309}{22}$ and median $= 14,$ then the value $( a - b{)}^{2}$ is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Class Frequency& Mid-point& \left({x}_{i}\right)$ ${f}_{i}{x}_{i}$
$0 - 6$ $a$ $\dfrac{0 + 6}{2} = 3$ $3a$
$6 - 12$ $b$ $\dfrac{6 + 12}{2} = 9$ $9b$

~ $N = \left(26 + a + b\right)$ ~ \left(504 + 3a + 9b\right)$

We know that, mean$= $\dfrac{∑ {f}_{i}{x}_{i}}{∑ {f}_{i}}

Given, mean$= $\dfrac{309}{22}

$⇒ $\dfrac{3a + 9b + 180 + 189 + 135}{a + b + 26} = \dfrac{309}{22}

$⇒ $\dfrac{504 + 3a + 9b}{a + b + 26} = \dfrac{309}{22}

$⇒ 66a + 198b + 11088 = 309a + 309b + 8034$

$⇒ 243a + 111b = 3054$

$⇒ 81a + 37b = 1018 . . . \left(1\right)$

Now, median$= 14,$~which lies in the interval~$12 - 18,$~thus~$12 - 18$~is the median class and we have~$= l + \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{N}{2} - c\right) \times h}{f},$

Where,~$l$~is the lower limit of the median class i.e.~$l = 12, c$~is the cumulative frequency of the class above the median class i.e.~$c = a + b, f$~is the frequency of the median class i.e.~$f = 12$~and~$h$~is the length of the interval i.e.~$h = 6 .$

Thus, we have~$12 + \left(\dfrac{\left(\dfrac{a + b + 26}{2}\right) - ( a + b )}{12}\right) \times6 = 14$

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{a + b + 26 - 2a - 2b}{2}\right)2 = 14 - 12$

$⇒ \dfrac{26 - a - b}{4} =2$

$⇒ 26 - a - b = 8$

$⇒ a + b = 18 . . . \left($2\right)$

On solving the equations \left(1\right)$~and~\left(2\right),$~we get~$a = 8, b = 10 .$

$∴ \left(a - b\right)2 = \left(8 - 10\right)2 = 4 .$

$
